newsitem.title: INDIA: India suspends payments to ONGC - paper.
newsitem.headline: India suspends payments to ONGC - paper.

text.p: An Indian newspaper said on Tuesday that the government had temporarily suspended payments to Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd (ONGC) for its crude petroleum sales due to a large deficit in the oil pool subsidy account.
The Economic Times said the suspension could last for "a couple of months" but that the state-run oil company was prepared for a hiatus as long as six months.
Weekly settlements to all refining companies including Indian Oil Corp Ltd (IOC) have also been cut, the business daily said.
Current outstandings to IOC are some 48 billion rupees, and they are projected to rise to 90 billion by end-March if settlements are not resumed, it said.
ONGC, IOC and government officials were not available for comment.
The government reimburses oil firms for the difference between what they pay to import crude and what domestic refiners pay them.
Petroleum Ministry officials estimate that the oil pool deficit is expected to touch 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) against 57 billion rupees last year.
The business daily said ONGC received its last payment from the government on November 11 from the pool account, for the month of October.
It said ONGC was demanding bank interest rates on deferred payments. The government pays the company about 2.7 billion rupees every month, the newspaper said.
Last week share prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange were hit by reports that an increase in petroleum prices seemed certain.
Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was quoted on Sunday as saying the government was considering raising the prices of petroleum products to cover the burgeoning cost of petrol subsidies.
"The events have overtaken us," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Chidambaram as telling TVI Network.
